title: The Wafer Is the New Battleground: Soitec CPO René Jonker on Building AI from the Substrate Up
gist: In a SEMICON West 2026 interview, Soitec CPO René Jonker argues that engineered substrates add properties at the cheapest point in the chain, with Photonics-SOI for co-packaged optics in AI data centers now driving growth after RF-SOI made Soitec dominant in 5G front ends. Soitec's stock rose more than sixfold from January to early October 2026, and the company is extending into SiC (SmartSiC), RF-GaN and smaller-geometry FD-SOI.

insights.claim: Soitec stock on Euronext Paris rose more than sixfold in 2026: $100 invested in January 2026 was worth more than $600 by early October.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: The market has re-rated Soitec as an AI beneficiary.
insights.quote: an investor who put $100 into its stock in January 2026 was holding more than $600 by early October

insights.claim: Soitec was spun out of CEA-Leti in 1992 to commercialize Smart Cut, which uses ion implantation and wafer bonding to transfer a nanometers-thin monocrystalline silicon layer onto an insulating substrate to make silicon-on-insulator wafers.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Smart Cut IP is the core moat underlying all of Soitec's platforms.
insights.locator: Soitec was spun out of CEA-Leti

insights.claim: Soitec's early growth came from SOI deals with AMD and IBM, but customer concentration and a detour into solar caused turbulence in the 2000s before a 2010s turnaround built on RF-SOI for smartphone front-end modules.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Soitec's history shows customer-concentration and diversification risk.

insights.claim: Soitec sits at the bottom of the value chain: foundries and IDMs such as TSMC, GlobalFoundries, STMicroelectronics, Samsung Foundry and UMC buy its wafers, and fabless firms such as Qualcomm, Apple, Broadcom, MediaTek and NXP specify Soitec platforms in their designs.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Design-in by fabless customers drives demand pull through foundries, making Soitec sticky.
insights.locator: Soitec is neither a foundry nor

insights.claim: As transistor scaling runs into leakage, parasitic capacitance and thermal limits, bulk silicon becomes the bottleneck, and a buried oxide layer under thin silicon often cuts power by 30 to 50 percent without a node shrink.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Substrate engineering offers power gains that otherwise require costly node migrations.
insights.quote: often cutting power by 30 to 50 percent without a node shrink
insights.locator: That position matters more every year.

insights.claim: Engineered substrates let suppliers add properties to silicon at the earliest stage so foundries do not need complicated processing to reach similar performance.
insights.speaker: René Jonker
insights.so_what: Value is migrating down the stack to materials suppliers.
insights.quote: By providing a substrate, you can add properties to silicon at a very early stage.
insights.locator: Jonker puts the formula in one sentence.

insights.claim: RF-SOI displaced competing technologies in mobile front-end modules by eliminating bulk silicon parasitics, made Soitec the dominant supplier, and now sits in RF switches and low-noise amplifiers in practically every 5G phone and Wi-Fi module.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: RF-SOI is a mature cash-generating franchise tied to smartphone volumes.

insights.claim: Soitec now runs five main substrate platforms, each built to solve a problem that is hard to fix further down the chain: RF-SOI, Photonics-SOI, FD-SOI, Power-SOI and Piezoelectric-on-Insulator.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Diversified platforms reduce Soitec's dependence on smartphone RF.
insights.locator: “That’s a little bit behind us now,”

insights.claim: Photonics-SOI is now Soitec's main growth driver, described as the new gold, because AI cluster interconnect is moving from copper to fiber and Photonics-SOI provides the electron-to-photon interface that underpins co-packaged optics in AI data centers.
insights.speaker: René Jonker
insights.so_what: Soitec is a picks-and-shovels play on co-packaged optics adoption.
insights.quote: “It’s now seen as the new gold,” Jonker says.

insights.claim: Silicon is only an okay waveguide material and indium phosphide performs better, but silicon photonics wins because the whole industry is set up for silicon and indium phosphide is difficult to work with.
insights.speaker: René Jonker
insights.so_what: Manufacturing ecosystem advantages favor silicon photonics over InP-based optics.
insights.quote: The whole industry is basically set up for silicon, and indium phosphide is a difficult material to begin with.

insights.claim: FD-SOI cuts leakage and compute power and supports back-biasing to trade speed against power on the fly, and is used in automotive radar, IoT microcontrollers and edge devices; Power-SOI serves high-voltage automotive and industrial circuits and POI targets acoustic RF filters for 5G and 6G.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Soitec's mid-portfolio gives exposure to auto, industrial and edge markets.

insights.claim: Demand for specialized materials such as gallium nitride and silicon carbide that enable features classical silicon cannot will keep growing, and the industry will see more and more kinds of materials.
insights.speaker: René Jonker
insights.so_what: Compound-semiconductor materials suppliers have a secular tailwind.
insights.quote: For me it is very clear: we will see more and more different kinds of materials.
insights.locator: The bigger shift, in Jonker’s view

insights.claim: Soitec's SmartSiC reuses a single-crystal silicon carbide donor wafer many times by bonding a thin layer onto a conductive base, lowering the cost of SiC power devices for EV inverters.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Lower-cost SiC substrates could pressure incumbent SiC wafer suppliers.

insights.claim: Soitec is developing RF-GaN on insulator for 6G power amplifiers and aerospace, and moving FD-SOI to smaller geometries for energy-conscious on-device AI in phones and wearables.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: Pipeline products extend Soitec into 6G and edge AI.

insights.claim: Soitec's direct substrate competition comes mostly from GlobalWafers, which Jonker says has or used to have access to Soitec IP, but he does not see GlobalWafers at Soitec's level today.
insights.speaker: René Jonker
insights.so_what: GlobalWafers is the main supplier-side threat to Soitec's share.
insights.quote: has or used to have access to our IP

insights.claim: The more important competition is between technologies: an FD-SOI customer could instead choose FinFET at TSMC, but FinFET is not very power efficient, giving designers who want to win on power a reason to pick FD-SOI.
insights.speaker: René Jonker
insights.so_what: FD-SOI adoption depends on power-sensitive designs choosing it over TSMC FinFET.
insights.quote: FinFET technology is not super efficient in terms of power usage
insights.locator: The more interesting competition is between

insights.claim: Soitec's substrates rarely win on raw physics alone; they win by adding a new property into a silicon-built manufacturing world at the cheapest point in the chain, and in the AI era every watt and bit moved between chips makes the wafer a design decision.
insights.speaker: Lauro Rizzatti
insights.so_what: AI power and bandwidth constraints are turning substrate choice into a strategic lever.
